about: Statements this site offered as citable before 2026-11-28 without receipts, kept so that anyone who cited one can see what happened to it. None of them is safe to cite. needs_reproduction: may come back once recomputed by a published script with a receipt. retired: will not come back in this form.

items.text: In 2025, FHA denial rates across 11 major lenders ranged from 6.5% (CrossCountry, lowest) to 52.3% (NewRez, highest) — an ~8x spread on the same federal loan program.
items.reason: Both ends disagree with the receipted rates (CrossCountry 6.2%, NewRez 52.8%). Replaced by the receipted range in data/citable.json.

items.text: The lender with the HIGHEST 2025 FHA denial rate among major originators is NewRez at 52.3%. The lowest is CrossCountry at 6.5%.
items.reason: Same figures as above; the receipted rates are 52.8% and 6.2%.

items.text: The deepest single denial cell in 2025 FHA records: Rocket Mortgage, DTI 48-50 x CLTV 90-95%, 97.6% denial rate (n=84).
items.reason: Computed once by a script that is not published; the highest of many small cells. See /black-hole-lender.html (provisional research note).

items.text: FRC Denial Climate Index 2025: 54.3/100 (NEUTRAL). 2023 was the tightest credit year of the era at 66/100; 2021 the loosest at 21/100 — a 3x climate difference for an identical borrower.
items.reason: A composite index without a published computation or receipt; 'for an identical borrower' states something an index of many applications cannot show.

items.text: At the median first-time-buyer down payment (10%, CLTV 90-94), the denial spread between major FHA lenders is ~79 percentage points (16.5% to 95.2%) — versus ~16 points at 20% down. Lower down payment makes lender choice ~5x more consequential.
items.reason: Frames a spread between lenders' applicant pools as the value of choosing a lender; figures not receipted.

items.text: Lender DTI cliffs differ sharply: one major lender's denial rate jumps ~+15 percentage points across DTI 44-45, while another's moves only +1.4pp.
items.reason: Cell-level figures without receipts, cell sizes or the number of cells compared.

items.text: Texas home prices turned negative in 2026 (-0.1% YoY) for the first time in the FHFA state series, while California sits near-flat (+0.8%).
items.reason: An FHFA figure without the release, quarter or receipt; 'for the first time in the series' not shown.

items.text: FHA denial rates predict FHA delinquency rates two years ahead (r=+0.618).
items.reason: A correlation without its n, series, years or method; 'predict' claims more than a correlation shows.

items.text: Unemployment correlates inversely with mortgage denial rates (r=-0.696) — the Recession Paradox.
items.reason: A correlation without its n, series, years or method.

items.text: Fed SLOOS survey responses show near-zero correlation with actual HMDA denial behavior (r=-0.150).
items.reason: A correlation without its n, series, years or method.

items.text: Rocket Mortgage's FHA denial rate jumps +54.9pp above 85% LTV; Mr. Cooper's jumps +1.7pp (2025 HMDA).
items.reason: Cell-level figures without receipts or cell sizes; part of a jump above 85% can be program limits (see /corrections.html#2026-11-28-legacy-research-pages).

items.text: Identical high-risk FHA profiles face 26.7% denial at Mr. Cooper vs 91.2% at Rocket — a 64.5pp spread.
items.reason: Presents two lenders' applicant pools as the same applicant; figures not receipted.

items.text: Shock Beta: pre-shock volatility predicted lender tightening response at r=+0.946; placebo easing episode confirmed at r=-0.605.
items.reason: The scores do not reproduce from their own data file (see /corrections.html#2026-11-28-legacy-research-pages).

items.text: UWM's FHA denial rate rose from 16.2% (2022) to 21.8% (2025) — a 35% increase.
items.reason: The receipted 2025 rate is 21.4%; the 2022 figure has no receipt.

items.text: Lender table: CrossCountry 6.5, Guild 8.6, Planet Home 18.4, UWM 21.8, Freedom 24.2, PennyMac 24.5, Mr. Cooper 25.8, Rocket 31.0, loanDepot 37.8, Wells Fargo 47.2, NewRez 52.3 (percent, 2025, with a rank of 11).
items.reason: Every one of the eleven rates differed from its receipt, by up to 4.3 points (Freedom 24.2 vs 19.9); replaced by the receipted rates in data/citable.json, alphabetical and without a rank.
